newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CITIC sees strong 1996 profit growth.
newsitem.headline: CITIC sees strong 1996 profit growth.

text.p: China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) president Qin Xiao said on Monday the group was on track for net profit growth of at least 25 to 30 percent in calendar 1996.
"(It was) a very good year...a better year for us, at least 25 to 30 percent increase in net profit," Xiao told reporters before an international trade conference to be held here this week.
CITIC, the state-owned trading giant based in Beijing, made group profits of 2.05 billion yuan in calendar 1995.

Underpinning the bullish prediction was steady growth in profits from the mainland-based CITIC Industrial Bank and better contributions from investments made by the group's Hong Kong-listed CITIC Pacific Ltd, Xiao said.
"Our bank (had a) very steady increase in profit along with the setting up of new branches," Xiao said.
CITIC Industrial Bank is the main contributor to the group's domestic earnings, netting profits of about one billion yuan last year.
Xiao did not give details of divisional earnings and made no mention of the bank's bad debt position.
In late October, CITIC group executive director Chang Zhenming said the bank had been able to hold bad debts steady but he did not specify a figure at the time.
Xiao heaped praise on Hong Kong-based CITIC Pacific.
"The vehicle in Hong Kong, they did a good job to make investments and deliver to (the group)," he said. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
